assumptions: 'Success rate' means attempt-level success rate: successful attempts divided by all attempts, with each retry counted as a separate attempt. Order-level and technical rates are shown alongside.

The period analysed is 17 September 2026, compared with the immediately preceding period of equal length (16 September 2026); the supporting evidence uses a wider 17-18 September window against a 10-16 September baseline.
Failure codes are reported per 100 attempts.
caveats: The comparison window in the evidence covers 17-18 September versus 10-16 September, so the headline figures cover two days rather than 17 September alone.
The hourly timeline evidence shown covers only the early hours of 16 September, so the exact start and end of the incident is not confirmed from this evidence.

facts.text: Attempt success rate fell 3.10pp from 90.07% (83,268 attempts, 10-16 Sep) to 86.98% (22,790 attempts, 17-18 Sep). The change is statistically and practically significant.
The daily rate had been steady at about 89.2%-90.4% in the days before the drop, and the anomaly window is flagged as 17-18 September.
Among all segments scanned, acquirer Kestrel Bank concentrated the drop most strongly, with its rate falling from 90.03% to 78.49%.

Within Kestrel Bank, card methods dropped sharply: debit card from 86.42% to 56.31% (-30.11pp), credit card from 88.64% to 59.94% (-28.71pp), card EMI from 80.67% to 56.80% (-23.87pp). UPI, wallet and netbanking at Kestrel Bank did not change significantly.
For Kestrel Bank card payments, ACQ_TIMEOUT failures rose from 0.26 to 32.27 per 100 attempts (803 failures in the current window versus 22 in the baseline). Other failure codes were flat or lower.
Across all traffic, ACQ_TIMEOUT rose from 0.08 to 3.58 per 100 attempts (815 failures versus 69), the largest shift of any failure code.

Platform-wide, card EMI fell 9.52pp (82.59% to 73.07%), debit card fell 9.28pp (86.13% to 76.85%) and credit card fell 9.18pp (88.91% to 79.73%). UPI was essentially unchanged (93.09% to 92.95%) and wallet rose 1.93pp (91.58% to 93.51%).
The data-quality scan found no findings (0) for the analysed window.

response.headline: Success rate fell 3.10pp, from 90.07% to 86.98%, across 17-18 September versus the prior week. The drop is concentrated in card payments routed through Kestrel Bank, where acquirer timeouts surged.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Check with Kestrel Bank for incident reports for 17-18 September and review the hourly timeline of Kestrel card attempts to see exactly when timeouts started and ended.
hypotheses.rationale: The decline is isolated to Kestrel Bank's card methods, while its UPI, wallet and netbanking are unaffected. The failure mix is dominated by ACQ_TIMEOUT, a technical acquirer-side code, rather than issuer declines or customer drop-off.
hypotheses.text: A technical problem at Kestrel Bank (for example an outage, degraded connectivity or a capacity issue on its card processing path) caused card transactions to time out.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Review routing rules and the success rates of alternative acquirers for card traffic over the same window.
hypotheses.rationale: Other acquirers and non-card methods held steady, suggesting alternate routes were healthy, but routing capacity and cost have not been examined here.
hypotheses.text: Card traffic could be re-routed to other acquirers to limit impact during the incident.

recommendations.linked_fact_or_hypothesis: A technical problem at Kestrel Bank caused card transactions to time out.
recommendations.rationale: ACQ_TIMEOUT at Kestrel Bank card payments explains the drop, and only the acquirer can confirm the root cause.
recommendations.text: Escalate to Kestrel Bank to confirm the cause, the start and end time, and whether the timeouts are resolved.

recommendations.linked_fact_or_hypothesis: Within Kestrel Bank, card methods dropped sharply and ACQ_TIMEOUT surged.
recommendations.rationale: Kestrel card success rates fell to about 56%-60%, so re-routing would protect revenue, and a timeout alert would catch similar incidents sooner.
recommendations.text: Consider failing over or re-routing Kestrel Bank card traffic to alternate acquirers while the issue persists, and set up an alert on ACQ_TIMEOUT per 100 attempts by acquirer.

recommendations.linked_fact_or_hypothesis: Attempt success rate fell 3.10pp from 90.07% to 86.98%.
recommendations.rationale: Failed card attempts during the window may be recoverable if customers are nudged to retry.
recommendations.text: Quantify lost successful payments and prompt retries or customer comms for affected card orders.
